Preterite Tense (Pretérito Indefinido)
Completed actions at a specific point in the past
-ar: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron | -er/-ir: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron
Ayer compré un billete de tren.
ah-YEHR kohm-PREH oon bee-YEH-teh deh trehn
Yesterday I bought a train ticket.
El año pasado viajamos a Sevilla.
ehl AH-nyoh pah-SAH-doh byah-HAH-mohs ah seh-BEE-yah
Last year we traveled to Seville.
Imperfect Tense (Pretérito Imperfecto)
Habitual past actions, descriptions, and ongoing background
-ar: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban | -er/-ir: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían
Cuando era niño, jugaba en el parque.
KWAHN-doh EH-rah NEE-nyoh hoo-GAH-bah ehn ehl PAHR-keh
When I was a child, I used to play in the park.
Hacía mucho calor aquella tarde.
ah-SEE-ah MOO-choh kah-LOHR ah-KEH-yah TAHR-deh
It was very hot that afternoon.
Preterite vs Imperfect
Preterite = completed event with a clear endpoint. Imperfect = ongoing background, habit, or description in the past.
Reflexive Verbs (Verbos Reflexivos)
Actions the subject performs on themselves
me / te / se / nos / se + conjugated verb
Me levanto a las siete de la mañana.
meh leh-BAHN-toh ah lahs SYEH-teh deh lah mah-NYAH-nah
I get up at seven in the morning.
¿Cómo te llamas?
KOH-moh teh YAH-mahs
What is your name? (How do you call yourself?)
Direct Object Pronouns (lo, la, los, las)
Replacing a direct object noun to avoid repetition
me / te / lo / la / nos / los / las + conjugated verb
¿El libro? Lo leí ayer.
ehl LEE-broh? loh leh-EE ah-YEHR
The book? I read it yesterday.
Las llaves están aquí; las tengo yo.
lahs YAH-behs ehs-TAHN ah-KEE; lahs TEHN-goh yoh
The keys are here; I have them.
Estar + Gerundio (Present Progressive)
Actions happening right at this moment
estar (present/imperfect) + -ando (-ar) / -iendo (-er/-ir)
Estoy preparando la cena ahora.
ehs-TOY preh-pah-RAHN-doh lah SEH-nah ah-OH-rah
I am preparing dinner right now.
Estamos esperando el autobús.
ehs-TAH-mohs ehs-peh-RAHN-doh ehl ow-toh-BOOS
We are waiting for the bus.
Comparatives (más / menos / tan ... como)
Comparing qualities, quantities, and actions
más/menos + adj + que | tan + adj + como | tanto/a + noun + como
Madrid es más grande que Toledo.
mah-DREED ehs mahs GRAHN-deh keh toh-LEH-doh
Madrid is bigger than Toledo.
Este hotel es tan cómodo como el otro.
EHS-teh oh-TEHL ehs tahn KOH-moh-doh KOH-moh ehl OH-troh
This hotel is as comfortable as the other one.
Saber vs. Conocer
Two different verbs for 'to know'
saber (facts, information, how to + inf) | conocer (people, places, familiarity)
Sé hablar un poco de español.
seh ah-BLAHR oon POH-koh deh ehs-pah-NYOHL
I know how to speak a little Spanish.
¿Conoces Barcelona?
koh-NOH-sehs bahr-seh-LOH-nah
Do you know (have you been to) Barcelona?
